sources.note: results.tsv. The aggregator is MIT for its code and states it does not host the source lists. NIKL publishes its list under KOGL Type 1 (공공누리 제1유형), which permits commercial and derivative use with attribution. Levels only; the `explanation` column is a collocation hint and is unused.

sources.name: Open Yonsei Korean Vocabulary (Amulopapa67), a community companion to the six-volume Yonsei course, not affiliated with Yonsei University
sources.note: vol-01.json … vol-06.json. Definitions and text readings only. The project licenses its data CC BY-SA 3.0 and excludes textbook lessons, examples, audio and official artwork.

meta.note: Korean words are joined to definitions on the word. Where the join misses, the word still marks and has no definition, which the popover states. Homograph senses (가구03, 가구04) merge into one entry at the easiest level.
